approach: Add crates/athena-core/tests/study_instance_split.rs, modelled on learnings_recorded.rs. It is the spec-level check that complements the existing study-capability enforcement. It does not replace it. Three pure checks drive real-file tests and negative tests. (1) `instance_problems(id, files)` flags a code file anywhere under a studies/<id>/ directory (extension from a code-extension list, or the names Cargo.toml and build.rs) and a missing pin.json. Nested directories and non-code file types are allowed, as `StudyCapability::admit` allows them. (2) `capability_problems(sources, ids)` flags a cap-study source only when it names an instance by a specific reference: the path `studies/<id>` ending at an id boundary, or the quoted literal `"<id>"`. A bare substring is not flagged. (3) The spec-entry checks copied from learnings_recorded.rs. docs/spec.toml OLY-B-S1-02 then names three mechanisms. `StudyCapability::admit` (crates/athena-cap-study/src/lib.rs:114-151) keeps instance work in one studies/<id>/. The conventions test `every_study_follows_the_conventions_and_the_matching_one_validates` (rules.rs:1841) checks every instance. The new test is the athena-core check. The measure names the new command and `cargo test -p athena-cap-study`, and ends `status: not shown`, because fresh context per instance and gap-fix-and-recheck cannot be shown from files. CHANGELOG gets an entry. xtask/shard-timings.txt gets one data line, because the xtask timings test needs it.

decisions.choice: Keep the athena-core static test as the spec-level check and cite the existing enforcement in the mechanism text. Name `StudyCapability::admit` (lib.rs:114-151, tested at lib.rs:256-309) and the per-instance conventions test in rules.rs (`Loaded::read` at 1498-1506 requires pin.json and five other files; `conventions` at 1613 checks pin study_id; the test at 1841 runs over every studies/<id>/). The test's doc comment says it complements them and shares the rule 'instance work is data under studies/<id>/ with a pin' with them.
decisions.reason: Finding 2: the instance split is already enforced at runtime and in cap-study tests. The new test adds what they do not: that the reusable crate holds no instance reference, and that the spec entry is closed. athena-core cannot depend on cap-study (crate reach in docs/system-facts.md), so the mechanism text and measure cite those tests and the new test does not call them.

rejected.option: Record only the new test as the mechanism
rejected.why: It would understate the real enforcement and present a weaker snapshot as the whole mechanism.

rejected.option: Call admit or the conventions check from the new test
rejected.why: athena-core has no dependency on athena-cap-study, and adding one would create a cycle (cap-study depends on core).

rejected.option: Add a runtime check in the capability
rejected.why: One already exists (admit), and changing capability runtime behaviour is out of scope.

decisions.choice: Match an instance reference by two specific forms only: `studies/<id>` where the next character is not an id character (alphanumeric, `-`, `_`), and the quoted literal `"<id>"`. Do not match bare ids. Add negative tests with the id `athena`: the real cap-study sources (and a string containing `athena_core`, `athena-cap-study` and the word Athena) give no problem, while `studies/athena/x.json` and `"athena"` each give one. Also `studies/athena-extra` does not match id `athena`.
decisions.reason: Finding 3: a substring match would false-positive on short or common ids (`athena`, `model`, `pin`) that the requirement expects next. I grepped crates/athena-cap-study (all files, case-insensitive) for `"athena"`, `"hermes"`, `studies/athena`, `studies/hermes`, `"model"`, `"rules"` and `"pin"` and found no hit. The cap-study tests use fixture paths `studies/a`, `studies/s1`, `studies/b` (lib.rs:249-314), which are not real instance ids. The real test therefore passes today, and a later instance with a short id does not break it.

rejected.why: Finding 3: false positives on `athena_core`, `athena-cap-study` and ordinary words.
`work-handling` is the generic mechanism name used at rules.rs:861 and model.rs:1.

decisions.choice: Drop the extension whitelist and the nested-directory rule. Forbid only code: files under studies/<id>/ (recursively) with an extension in a code list (rs, sh, bash, py, js, ts, rb, go, c, h, cpp, java, pl) or named Cargo.toml or build.rs. The test header states that it shares with `admit` the rule that instance work is one studies/<id>/ directory, and shares nothing about file types, because admit limits none.
decisions.reason: Finding 4: `admit` accepts nested paths such as studies/a/sub/dir/x.json (lib.rs:267) and limits no file type. A stricter test would fail cargo test on a tree a legitimate study job produced. Tightening admit would change runtime behaviour and is out of scope.

rejected.option: Whitelist json and md and refuse nested directories
rejected.why: Finding 4: refuses layouts the capability accepts.
Changes the capability's runtime behaviour, which is out of scope.

decisions.reason: Acceptance criteria 2 and 3 name the pin and a missing-pin negative case, so the check stays. It is a one-line existence check that defers to rules.rs for content.

rejected.why: Contradicts acceptance criteria 2 and 3 as written.

steps: Create crates/athena-core/tests/study_instance_split.rs. Start with a //! doc comment: the requirement id, what is checked, that the test complements `StudyCapability::admit` (crates/athena-cap-study/src/lib.rs:114) and the rules.rs conventions test (rules.rs:1841), which rules it shares with them (instance work is data under one studies/<id>/ with a pin.json), and what is not shown (fresh context per instance, gap-fix-and-recheck). Add constants REQUIREMENT="OLY-B-S1-02", TEST_COMMAND="cargo test -p athena-core --test study_instance_split" and CODE_EXTENSIONS. Copy `repo_file`, `owner_problem`, `measure_label_problem` from learnings_recorded.rs:24-29 and 153-163. Add `real_requirement`, which uses `athena_core::hestia::parse_spec` and finds the id.

Add `instance_problems(id: &str, files: &[String]) -> Vec<String>`. `files` are paths relative to studies/<id>/. It reports each file whose extension is in CODE_EXTENSIONS or whose name is Cargo.toml or build.rs (any depth), and reports a missing top-level `pin.json`. Allow nested directories and other file types.

Add `capability_problems(sources: &[(String, String)], ids: &[String]) -> Vec<String>`. It reports each (file, id) where the text contains `studies/<id>` not followed by an id character (alphanumeric, `-`, `_`) or contains the quoted literal `"<id>"`. Add helpers that list studies/*/ directories and their files recursively, and read the files of crates/athena-cap-study/src and prompts/ recursively.

Add the real-file tests `every_study_instance_holds_no_code_and_a_pin` (assert at least one instance, then an empty problem list per instance) and `the_study_capability_names_no_instance` (real sources against real ids; also against the hypothetical ids `athena` and `hermes`, which must give no problem).

Add negative tests as listed in demonstration 3: .rs and nested .sh in an instance; missing pin.json; `studies/<id>/` path reference; quoted-literal reference; `athena_core`, `athena-cap-study` and the prose word Athena passing for id `athena`; `studies/athena/x.json` and `"athena"` failing; `studies/athena-extra` passing for id `athena`; nested json and md allowed; measure without label; measure without command; wrong owner; mechanism `none` in spec_gaps. Each first asserts the clean input is empty.

Add `spec_entry_has_a_real_mechanism`: mechanism is not `none` and contains the test file path, `StudyCapability::admit` and `every_study_follows_the_conventions`; owner_problem, measure_problem and measure_label_problem are None; OLY-B-S1-02 is not in `spec_gaps`.

Edit docs/spec.toml at the OLY-B-S1-02 table. Set mechanism to `crates/athena-core/tests/study_instance_split.rs checks on the real files that every studies/<id>/ holds no code and has a pin.json and that crates/athena-cap-study names no instance; StudyCapability::admit (crates/athena-cap-study/src/lib.rs) refuses a study change outside one studies/<id>/ directory; the per-instance conventions test every_study_follows_the_conventions_and_the_matching_one_validates (crates/athena-cap-study/src/rules.rs) checks each instance; fresh context per instance and gap fix and re-check are not covered`. Keep owner = "Athena". Set measure to `Reusable study logic is in crates/athena-cap-study and instance data is in studies/<id>/, checked on the real files; cargo test -p athena-core --test study_instance_split; cargo test -p athena-cap-study; status: not shown`. Leave statement, kind, status and sources unchanged.
Add `athena-core --test study_instance_split 5.00` to xtask/shard-timings.txt next to the other athena-core test lines.

Add a CHANGELOG.md bullet at the top of `## [Unreleased]` / `### Added`, in the style of the OLY-B-A3-02 bullet: the requirement id, the test file, the existing mechanisms it cites, the `status: not shown` limit, the timings line, and that no runtime or prompt change was made.

Run `cargo fmt --all`, then `cargo test -p athena-core --test study_instance_split`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`. Fix any failure in the new or edited files.

risks.risk: Static checks do not show fresh context per instance or the gap-fix-and-recheck loop, so the requirement is only partly shown.
risks.mitigation: The measure ends `status: not shown`. The test doc, the mechanism text and the changelog state the limit. Studying Hermes and Athena is out of scope.

risks.risk: A later instance legitimately includes a file type on the code list, such as a .sh fixture, and the test blocks it.
risks.mitigation: The code-extension list is one constant. The message names the file and the rule. Other types and nested directories are allowed, as `admit` allows them.

risks.risk: A future instance id is short and appears as a quoted literal or `studies/<id>` in capability code or prompts.
risks.mitigation: Only those two specific forms are matched, so `athena_core` and ordinary words do not trigger it. A hit means the capability names an instance, which is what the requirement forbids. The message names the file and the id. The cap-study test fixtures use `studies/a`, `studies/b` and `studies/s1` (lib.rs:249-314), so a future instance with one of those ids would conflict. The producer notes this in the test comment.

risks.risk: The spec.toml edit is in a 211 KB file with long lines, so a wrong replace could hit another entry.
risks.mitigation: Edit only the OLY-B-S1-02 table (docs/spec.toml:2927-2934), anchored on `id = "OLY-B-S1-02"`. The parse tests catch a TOML error.

risks.risk: The new test duplicates part of the cap-study checks and the two drift apart.
risks.mitigation: The test checks only what the cap-study tests do not (no instance reference in the capability; code-free instance directories; spec entry closed) plus the pin.json existence minimum. The mechanism text cites the stronger checks by name.

demonstrations.method: Two real-file tests walk the real tree. `every_study_instance_holds_no_code_and_a_pin` lists studies/*/ recursively (asserting at least one instance) and calls `instance_problems`. `the_study_capability_names_no_instance` reads every file under crates/athena-cap-study/src and prompts/ and calls `capability_problems` with the directory names under studies/.

demonstrations.method: Negative unit tests call the same pure functions on in-memory input. Each asserts the clean input gives no problem, then the mutated input gives the specific problem: (a) a `helper.rs` and a nested `sub/run.sh` in an instance; (b) a listing without pin.json; (c) a source containing `studies/firstmate-work-handling/x.json`, and one containing `"firstmate-work-handling"`; (d) id `athena` against `athena_core`, `athena-cap-study` and prose 'Athena' gives none, against `studies/athena/` or `"athena"` gives one, and `studies/athena-extra` gives none for id `athena`; (e) a nested `sub/dir/x.json` and an `.md` file are not flagged; (f) a measure without `status: not shown`, a measure without the test command, a wrong owner, and mechanism `none` appearing in spec_gaps.
demonstrations.observes: Every mutated input yields exactly the expected problem string. Every clean or allowed input yields none. The test therefore fails if any check is removed or loosened, and does not refuse layouts that `admit` accepts (lib.rs:267).
demonstrations.fails_without: If `instance_problems` stopped flagging code files or missing pins, or `capability_problems` ignored the two reference forms, the matching negative test would see an empty list and fail. If it reverted to substring matching, the `athena_core` case would fail.
demonstrations.seam: The production checks are `instance_problems`, `capability_problems`, `owner_problem`, `measure_label_problem` and `athena_core::hestia::spec_gaps` (hestia.rs:1291). Fixtures are plain strings or a real requirement with one field changed. The logic under test is not in the fixtures. Added by plan steps 2 to 5; `spec_gaps` exists.
